record.context_brief: complexity of deciding existence of general (a,b)-supermatches
record.original_question: For the more general notion of an (a,b)-supermatch in Stable Roommates or Stable Marriage settings, is the decision problem in NP, and if so what is its precise computational complexity?

evidence.quote: However, for the more general case of (a, b)-supermatches, it is not even known whether the problem belongs to NP.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setting. In the Stable Marriage problem, an instance consists of two disjoint sets of agents (e.g., men and women) of equal size, each agent having a strict preference list ranking all agents of the opposite set. A matching M is a set of disjoint man–woman pairs covering all agents. A pair (m,w) not in M is blocking if m and w both strictly prefer each other to their partners in M. M is stable if it admits no blocking pair. In the Stable Roommates problem, agents form a single set of even size, each ranking all others, and stable matchings and blocking pairs are defined analogously.

Robustness notion. Fix positive integers a and b. Given a stable matching M, an (a,b)-supermatch is a stable matching M with the following property: for every set S of a pairs of M, there exists a stable matching M′ such that
 (i) every agent appearing in some pair of S is matched in M′ to a partner different from the one assigned in M, and
 (ii) M and M′ differ on at most a + b pairs in total (equivalently, repairing the a broken pairs of S causes at most b additional pairs of M to be broken).

Decision problem. (a,b)-SUPERMATCH: Given an instance I of Stable Marriage (resp. Stable Roommates) and positive integers a, b encoded in unary or binary, decide whether I admits an (a,b)-supermatch.

Question. Does (a,b)-SUPERMATCH belong to NP? If so, determine its precise computational complexity (in particular, whether it is NP-complete, and where it sits in the polynomial hierarchy otherwise).
artifact.status_search_result: The (1,1)-supermatch existence problem is known to be NP-complete (Genc et al., 2019), and polynomial-time procedures exist for verifying that a given matching is a (1,b)-supermatch in Stable Roommates. However, for the general (a,b)-supermatch existence problem, no search result establishes membership in NP, and the question of its exact complexity appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: An Approach to Robustness in the Stable Roommates Problem and Its Comparison with the Stable Marriage Problem
status_evidence.snippet: Polynomial procedure to verify a stable matching is a (1,b)-supermatch via reduced rotation poset; (1,1)-supermatch existence shown NP-complete.
status_evidence.claim: Existence of a (1,1)-supermatch is NP-complete; general (a,b) case not addressed.

status_evidence.title: Adapting stable matchings to evolving preferences
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses robustness variants of stable matching and computational complexity.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work on robustness of stable matchings; general (a,b)-supermatch complexity not resolved.
